Dadhīci
------------------------------------------
Dadhīci (also spelt as ‘Dadhīca’) was a great sage who willingly sacrificed his life to help the gods conquer their eternal foes, the असुरस्.
Once the gods deposited their various weapons with the sage दधीचि for safe custody. But they did not return in the stipulated time. Since the weapons were getting rusted and were crumbling, the sage dissolved them in water and drank the same. They got merged in his backbone making it immensely strong. When the gods, under the leadership of their king इन्द्र came back and asked for the return of their weapons, दधीचि told them what he had done. Since they requested for his backbone, out of which a great weapon could be made and with which their formidable foe, वृत्रासुर, could be killed, he immediately obliged them by giving up his body in योग. इन्द्र’s वज्रायुध (thunderbolt) was prepared out of it.
Dadhīci stands for the highest ideal of self-sacrifice for social good.
He was the son of Atharvaṇa and Śānti. The well-known sage पिप्पलाद of Upaniṣadic fame was his son.
See also INDRA and VAJRĀYUDHA.

dadhi
(‘that [which] sustains’)
------------------------------------------
Derived from the root ‘dhā’ (to support, to sustain) the word ‘dadhi’ represents curds (curdled milk or yoghurt), since, perhaps, it is considered to be a better ड़ोओद् item than milk in sustaining the health of the body.
It has important uses in वेदिच् सच्रिड़िचेस्. It is used to curdle fresh, hot, milk which is used as oblation and also consumed by the sacrificer in the Darśa sacrifice. So also in the आग्रयण rite. In the animal sacrifice (Paśubandha) it is utilised to prepare पृषदाज्य (a mixture of curds and ghee) used for sprinkling over the immolated animal. It is expected to be consumed by the sacrificer in the दीक्षा rite (consecration of the sacrificer in a सोम sacrifice).
‘Dadhigraha’ refers to the drawing of curds offered to प्रजापति just before the morning pressing of the सोम juice.
‘Dadhigharma’ is a beverage of hot milk and curdled milk poured into a warm pot by the अध्वर्यु priest and used as a libation at the midday pressing of the सोम juice in a सोमयाग. ‘Dadhimantha’ is a beverage of grains (saktu) mixed with curds, also used in sacrifices.
